boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Union College
boards.description: Ten Schenectady food stops with posted late hours, selected for under-21-safe pickup, delivery, or dine-in options.

cards.title: Marino's Pizza & Restaurant
cards.subtitle: 1301 State St, Schenectady
cards.notes: Check the posted day before leaving: the restaurant lists midnight closing Monday–Thursday, 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday, and 11 p.m. Sunday.
cards.short_summary: A State Street restaurant with late posted closing times on most evenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Marino's lists hours until midnight Monday–Thursday, 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday, and 11 p.m. Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Mon–Thu 4 p.m.–midnight; Fri–Sat 4 p.m.–1 a.m.; Sun 3–11 p.m.; closed Tuesday. Confirm before travel.

cards.title: Pizza King
cards.subtitle: 124 Jay St, Schenectady
cards.notes: Use the restaurant's ordering page to confirm availability; it posts pickup and delivery until 2 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: Downtown pizza pickup and delivery with weekend hours extending to 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza King's official ordering page lists Friday and Saturday pickup and delivery hours of 10:30 a.m.–2 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Posted pickup and delivery hours are until 2 a.m. Friday and Saturday; Sunday–Thursday hours end at 9 p.m. Confirm before travel.

cards.title: State Street Pizzeria
cards.subtitle: 735 State St, Schenectady
cards.notes: Plan a pickup around the posted schedule: it lists midnight closing Monday–Thursday and 1 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A State Street pizza stop with nightly posted hours through midnight or later.
cards.evidence_claim: State Street Pizzeria lists hours until midnight Monday–Thursday and 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: 11 a.m.–midnight Monday–Thursday and 11 a.m.–1 a.m. Friday–Saturday; closed Sunday. Confirm before travel.

cards.title: Sicilian Pizzeria
cards.subtitle: 1505 Van Vranken Ave, Schenectady
cards.notes: The online ordering page posts cooking hours through 11 p.m. most days and midnight Friday and Saturday; check it before ordering.
cards.short_summary: Van Vranken Avenue pizza and delivery service with posted late-week hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Sicilian Pizzeria lists cooking hours until 11 p.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday, and midnight Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Sicilian Pizzeria | View Menu & Order Online
cards.access_notes: Posted cooking hours run to 11 p.m. most days and midnight Friday–Saturday; delivery estimates and availability can vary.

cards.title: Herbie's Burgers
cards.subtitle: 175 Jay St, Schenectady
cards.notes: For a downtown food run, use the official order page: it lists the Schenectady location as open daily from 11 a.m. to 2 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A Jay Street burger counter with official daily hours until 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Herbie's official order page lists its 175 Jay Street Schenectady location as open daily 11 a.m.–2 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official page posts daily 11 a.m.–2 a.m. for the 175 Jay Street location. Check ordering availability before heading out.

cards.title: Denny's on Nott Terrace
cards.subtitle: 60 Nott Terrace, Schenectady
cards.notes: Check the location page for the day you go; it posts midnight closing on several days and 24-hour service Thursday through Sunday.
cards.short_summary: A Nott Terrace diner with posted midnight and 24-hour operating windows.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny's official location page lists 24-hour restaurant hours Thursday through Sunday and midnight closing on other listed days.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists 24-hour hours Thursday–Sunday and 6 a.m.–midnight on Monday–Wednesday; holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on Altamont Avenue
cards.subtitle: 1820 Altamont Ave, Schenectady
cards.notes: Use the location's delivery or carryout page before ordering; it posts midnight closing most days and 1 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Schenectady chain pizza location with posted delivery and carryout through midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut's 1820 Altamont Avenue location lists delivery and carryout until midnight Sunday–Thursday and 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Posted delivery and carryout hours end at midnight Sunday–Thursday and 1 a.m. Friday–Saturday. Confirm service before travel.

cards.title: Wendy's on Altamont Avenue
cards.subtitle: 1590 Altamont Ave, Schenectady
cards.notes: The official location page posts restaurant and drive-through service to 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Schenectady fast-food option with official restaurant and drive-through hours after midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy's official page for 1590 Altamont Avenue lists restaurant and drive-through hours until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Posted restaurant and drive-through hours: until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday; holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Sicilian Pizza and Gyro
cards.subtitle: 1138 State St, Schenectady
cards.notes: Check the restaurant's ordering site before setting out: it posts 11 p.m. closing Monday–Thursday and Sunday, plus midnight Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A State Street pizza and halal-food stop with posted midnight weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Sicilian Pizza and Gyro lists hours until 11 p.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday, and midnight Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: Sicilian Pizza and Gyro Schenectady | About Us
cards.access_notes: Posted restaurant hours run until 11 p.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday, and midnight Friday–Saturday. Delivery is stated as available up to 3 miles.

cards.title: Mike's Hot Dogs
cards.subtitle: 1135 Erie Blvd, Schenectady
cards.notes: For an earlier late-evening stop, the restaurant's own site lists Monday–Saturday hours from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.; verify before going.
cards.short_summary: An Erie Boulevard counter-service restaurant with posted 10 p.m. weekday and Saturday closing.
cards.evidence_claim: Mike's Hot Dogs lists restaurant hours of 6 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 6 a.m.–8 p.m. Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official posted hours are 6 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 6 a.m.–8 p.m. Sunday. Confirm before travel.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Union spaces for studying, making, attending campus events, and connecting with other students.

cards.title: Reamer Campus Center
cards.subtitle: Student services, dining, WRUC, and Concordiensis
cards.notes: Use Reamer as a practical between-class stop: meet collaborators, visit student-resource offices, or check the posted activity around the building.
cards.short_summary: A central campus building that combines student services, food, media, and informal gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: Union identifies Reamer as home to student offices, dining services, WRUC, and Concordiensis, with a back patio used for lunch and studying.
cards.access_notes: Located on Union’s campus; dining, offices, and other services have their own availability and requirements.

cards.title: Schaffer Library Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, first floor
cards.notes: Bring a research question or group assignment and choose the Learning Commons when conversation and shared work fit better than a silent floor.
cards.short_summary: A student-focused library area for independent and collaborative research.
cards.evidence_claim: Union describes the Learning Commons as a student-focused area supporting independent and collaborative research.
cards.access_notes: Library entry requires a current Union College ID; use the library’s posted hours and study-zone guidance.

cards.title: Nott Memorial
cards.subtitle: Mandeville and Wikoff galleries; campus event space
cards.notes: Check the event and gallery listings before heading inside; the building also has third-floor sitting areas for a quieter reading break.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark used for talks, readings, special events, gallery viewing, and study.
cards.evidence_claim: Union states that the Nott hosts talks, readings, special events, Mandeville Gallery exhibitions, and third-floor study seating near the Wikoff Student Gallery.
cards.access_notes: Event and gallery access can vary; confirm the relevant campus listing before visiting.

cards.title: Jackson's Garden
cards.subtitle: Eight-acre campus garden
cards.notes: Take a short reset along the creek or gazebo, then bring a sketchbook, book, or picnic for a low-key outdoor break between commitments.
cards.short_summary: A campus garden with paths, plants, sculptures, a creek, and a gazebo.
cards.evidence_claim: Union describes Jackson’s Garden as an eight-acre garden where students sketch, paint, picnic, practice yoga, and read.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and seasonal access apply; enter through the campus garden entrance and respect the landscape.

cards.title: Old Chapel
cards.subtitle: Language Center, International Programs, and event space
cards.notes: Look for public campus programs here, or use a scheduled Language Center visit to practice with the resources and conversation support available upstairs.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus building that brings together student resources, events, language learning, and international-program support.
cards.evidence_claim: Union says Old Chapel hosts campus events and contains International Programs and the Language Center, which supports language learning and conversation partners.
cards.access_notes: Language Center appointments and event access vary; check the relevant office or event information first.

cards.title: Feigenbaum Center for Visual Arts
cards.subtitle: Studios, galleries, and maker resources
cards.notes: Visit an exhibition or attend a listed art talk, then ask the department about course-linked studios and maker resources before planning project work.
cards.short_summary: A visual-arts building with studios, exhibition spaces, and hands-on making facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Union lists drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, photography, digital-arts, and maker facilities in the Feigenbaum Center for Visual Arts.
cards.source_title: Visual Arts Facilities and Resources | Union College
cards.access_notes: Studio and equipment use may be tied to courses or department permissions; gallery and event availability varies.

cards.title: Crowell and West Galleries
cards.subtitle: Feigenbaum Center for Visual Arts
cards.notes: Watch the visual-arts calendar for exhibitions, artist talks, workshops, or receptions, and give yourself time to view the student and professional work closely.
cards.short_summary: Paired gallery spaces that present professional-artist and student exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Union reports that the Crowell and West Galleries host professional and student exhibitions and regularly host receptions, workshops, and artist talks.
cards.source_title: Visual Arts Facilities and Resources | Union College
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions and events change during the academic year; verify the current visual-arts schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Henle Dance Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Theater and Dance performance venue
cards.notes: Use the current-season calendar to find a studio performance, master class, lecture-demonstration, or discussion that fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus dance venue hosting performances and program events.
cards.evidence_claim: Union’s current Theater and Dance season lists performances and campus events in Henle Dance Pavilion, including master classes and lecture-demonstrations.
cards.source_title: Current Season | Theater & Dance | Union College
cards.access_notes: Admission and participation vary by event; review the current-season listing for the specific program.

cards.title: Wold Student Gallery
cards.subtitle: Peter Irving Wold Center, first floor
cards.notes: Pair a pass through the Wold Center with time to view the student work on display, then follow Visual Arts announcements for changing exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor gallery where Union student artists exhibit work.
cards.evidence_claim: Union states that the Wold Student Gallery displays work by annual Visual Arts prize winners and other student artists for weeks to months.
cards.source_title: Visual Arts Facilities and Resources | Union College
cards.access_notes: Artwork rotates; check Visual Arts communications for current exhibition details.

cards.title: Kenney Community Center
cards.subtitle: Community engagement and outreach
cards.notes: Start with the center’s current opportunities if you want a structured way to connect a campus interest with a Schenectady-area volunteer commitment.
cards.short_summary: A Union center connected to student volunteer activity and community outreach.
cards.evidence_claim: Union identifies the Kenney Community Center as part of its community outreach work and reports student involvement in its volunteer activities.
cards.source_title: Four students honored for volunteer service | Union College
cards.access_notes: Volunteer opportunities and participation requirements vary; contact the center for current options.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten current, documented no-admission activities at Union College and nearby Schenectady sites.

cards.title: Browse Mandeville Gallery
cards.subtitle: Nott Memorial, Union College
cards.notes: Meet upstairs in the Nott Memorial, move through the current exhibition together, and use one artwork as a prompt for a low-key conversation.
cards.short_summary: A seven-day-a-week, public art stop inside Union’s Nott Memorial.
cards.evidence_claim: Union states that Mandeville Gallery is on the Nott Memorial’s second floor and is free and open to the public seven days a week.
cards.source_title: Union Staff Resources | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public seven days a week, per Union; check the gallery’s current exhibition details before going.

cards.title: Take the Hervé Koubi master class
cards.subtitle: Henle Dance Pavilion, Union College — Oct. 16
cards.notes: Bring a friend to the 5 p.m. master class, arrive ready to move, and confirm any participation guidance with the Theater and Dance department.
cards.short_summary: A free public dance master class during Union’s Stephanie C. Davis Dance Residency.
cards.evidence_claim: Union lists a 5–6:15 p.m. Compagnie Hervé KOUBI master class in Henle Dance Pavilion on Oct. 16, 2026, and says both on-campus events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Current Season | Theater & Dance | Union College
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for Friday, Oct. 16, 2026, 5–6:15 p.m.; Union says it is free and open to the public.

cards.title: Catch the Hervé Koubi demo
cards.subtitle: Henle Dance Pavilion, Union College — Oct. 16
cards.notes: Stay or return for the 6:30 p.m. lecture-demonstration, then compare notes on the movement, capoeira, and urban-dance elements described by Union.
cards.short_summary: A free public artist lecture-demonstration following the residency master class.
cards.evidence_claim: Union lists a 6:30–7:30 p.m. Compagnie Hervé KOUBI lecture/demonstration in Henle Dance Pavilion on Oct. 16, 2026, and says both events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Current Season | Theater & Dance | Union College
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for Friday, Oct. 16, 2026, 6:30–7:30 p.m.; Union says it is free and open to the public.

cards.entity_name: The First Adirondackers: 12,000 Years of Indigenous Peoples in the ADK Uplands
cards.title: Hear “The First Adirondackers”
cards.subtitle: Old Chapel, Union College — Sept. 18
cards.notes: Register for this one-time Old Chapel presentation, then linger with friends to discuss the archaeology, natural science, and oral-history perspectives.
cards.short_summary: A free public talk on 12,000 years of Indigenous presence in the Adirondack uplands.
cards.evidence_claim: Union’s UCALL page lists this Sept. 18, 2026 Old Chapel event as free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Courses and Registration | UCALL | Union College
cards.access_notes: Friday, Sept. 18, 2026, at 5:30 p.m. in Old Chapel; the listing says free and open to all and provides registration.

cards.entity_name: Civic Engagement and Volunteerism: Making an Impact in Your Community
cards.title: Join the civic-engagement session
cards.subtitle: College Park Hall Ballroom, Union College — Sept. 28
cards.notes: Register for the session and go with a friend; use its local-government, citizen-science, nonprofit, and political-service examples to compare next steps.
cards.short_summary: A free public session about finding manageable local service pathways.
cards.evidence_claim: Union’s UCALL page lists this Sept. 28, 2026 College Park Hall Ballroom session as free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Courses and Registration | UCALL | Union College
cards.access_notes: Monday, Sept. 28, 2026, 9:30–11:30 a.m.; the listing says free and open to all and provides registration.

cards.entity_name: Schenectady County Outdoor Summer Movie Night at River Road Park
cards.title: Bring a blanket to River Road Park
cards.subtitle: River Road Park, Niskayuna — Aug. 19
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or lawn chair, meet at the park before the screening, and settle in for a no-ticket outdoor movie night with friends.
cards.short_summary: One of Schenectady County’s four free August outdoor movie nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Schenectady County says its August movie nights are free and include a screening at River Road Park in Niskayuna.
cards.source_title: Schenectady County Announces Lineup of Free and Family-Friendly Events for Summer Break
cards.access_notes: Listed for Aug. 19, 2026. Bring your own seating; the County describes the August movie nights as free.

cards.entity_name: Schenectady County Outdoor Summer Movie Night at Mabee Farm Historic Site
cards.title: Watch a movie at Mabee Farm
cards.subtitle: Mabee Farm Historic Site, Rotterdam Junction — Aug. 24
cards.notes: Pack a blanket or lawn chairs, arrive early to choose a spot, and enjoy the outdoor screening without needing an admission purchase.
cards.short_summary: A County-sponsored, all-ages outdoor movie night at the historic farm.
cards.evidence_claim: Schenectady County lists its Aug. 24, 2026 outdoor movie night at Mabee Farm Historic Site as free and open to all ages.
cards.source_title: Schenectady County Outdoor Summer Movie Night
cards.access_notes: Aug. 24, 2026, 7:30–9:30 p.m.; the movie begins at 8 p.m. The County says it is free and open to all ages.

cards.title: Listen at Jazz on Jay
cards.subtitle: Jay Square, downtown Schenectady
cards.notes: Meet at Jay Square for a Thursday set, bring a seat if you want one, and keep the plan simple by skipping purchases from nearby businesses.
cards.short_summary: Free Thursday outdoor jazz concerts in downtown Schenectady through late August.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Jazz on Jay site says its 2026 schedule offers free outdoor concerts at Jay Square in Schenectady.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 series runs Thursdays through Aug. 27 at Jay Square; official site identifies the concerts as free.

cards.title: Catch a Music Haven set
cards.subtitle: Music Haven Stage, Central Park, Schenectady
cards.notes: Check the remaining program, bring a blanket or lawn chair, and make an easy evening of the free outdoor performance in Central Park.
cards.short_summary: A free summer series of music, comedy, film, and community events in Central Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Music Haven states that its 2026 Summer Series in Schenectady’s Central Park is a free season running July 12 through Aug. 28.
cards.access_notes: The stated 2026 season runs through Aug. 28; review the program for the remaining dates and weather updates.

cards.entity_name: Hon. Karen B. Johnson Main Library Meeting Rooms
cards.title: Attend an open library meeting
cards.subtitle: Hon. Karen B. Johnson Main Library, Schenectady
cards.notes: Check the library calendar for an open noncommercial gathering, then use the meeting rooms as a no-admission setting for a social, cultural, or educational event.
cards.short_summary: Public meetings at the County library cannot charge admission or take a collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Schenectady County Public Library says its meeting rooms support social, cultural, and educational activities; qualifying use is free and no admission charge or collection is allowed.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Room | Schenectady County Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use the library calendar to find an event open to the public. The room policy prohibits admission charges and collections.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, source-documented study environments within Schaffer Library, from silent reading rooms to small-group and media-equipped spaces.

cards.title: Lally Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, first floor
cards.notes: Set up behind the first-floor glass doors when you need a no-conversation, no-cellphone-use reading session.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study room with strict sound rules.
cards.evidence_claim: Schaffer designates the Lally Reading Room, behind glass doors on the first floor, as a Quiet Study area where conversations and cellphone use are prohibited.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Schaffer Library entrance requires a Union ID; follow the Quiet Study rules posted for this room.

cards.entity_name: Schaffer Library Third Floor Quiet Study
cards.title: Third Floor Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, third floor
cards.notes: Bring reading or solo work upstairs and keep phones silent; this entire floor is designated for quiet study.
cards.short_summary: A whole-floor quiet zone for focused individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Schaffer Library identifies its entire third floor as a Quiet Study zone with no conversations or cellphone use.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Schaffer Library entrance requires a Union ID; no conversation or cellphone use is permitted in Quiet Study zones.

cards.title: Second Floor Stacks Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, second floor behind glass doors
cards.notes: Use the stacks behind the glass doors for reading that benefits from silence and a nearby circulating-book collection.
cards.short_summary: Quiet seating beside the second-floor book stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Schaffer designates the second-floor stacks behind the glass doors as Quiet Study, and its floor directory places circulating books on the second floor.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Schaffer Library entrance requires a Union ID; Quiet Study permits neither conversations nor cellphone use.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, first floor
cards.notes: Choose this first-floor area for a project that benefits from research workstations and conversation-permitted collaboration.
cards.short_summary: The library’s open-collaboration area with research workstations.
cards.evidence_claim: Union describes the first-floor Learning Commons as student-focused support for independent and collaborative research; Schaffer designates it an Open Collaboration zone.
cards.access_notes: Schaffer Library entrance requires a Union ID; conversation is permitted in the first-floor Open Collaboration zone.

cards.title: Café-Styled Booths
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, first and second floors
cards.notes: Meet a partner at one of the library’s booths on the first or second floor and keep the conversation appropriate to the zone.
cards.short_summary: Built-in booth seating on two library floors.
cards.evidence_claim: Schaffer Library lists café-styled booths as available on its first and second floors.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Schaffer Library entrance requires a Union ID; the second floor is quiet collaboration except behind its glass doors.

cards.title: Group Study Room 14
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, basement
cards.notes: Use this basement room for a private small-group session; plan for first-come, first-served use rather than a reservation.
cards.short_summary: A basement private group-study room.
cards.evidence_claim: Schaffer identifies Group Study Room 14 in the basement, and its building policy says basement study rooms are first-come, first-served.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Schaffer Library entrance requires a Union ID; basement study rooms are first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Group Study Room 15
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, basement
cards.notes: Bring a small team to this basement room for focused discussion, leaving the doorway clear for fire-safety compliance.
cards.short_summary: A separate basement room for private group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Schaffer identifies Group Study Room 15 in the basement; its building policy requires that study-room doors not be blocked.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Schaffer Library entrance requires a Union ID; basement study rooms are first-come, first-served and doorways must remain clear.

cards.title: Group Study Room 210
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use Room 210 for a private gathering; students needing media equipment receive priority in the library’s group-study rooms.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor private study room with media-use priority.
cards.evidence_claim: Schaffer lists Group Study Room 210 on the second floor and states that students requiring media equipment have priority in group-study rooms.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Schaffer Library entrance requires a Union ID; check room availability and yield priority to students who require media equipment.

cards.title: Learning Lab, Room 232
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use the modular tables and chairs for group work when no scheduled library instruction session is using Room 232.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, reconfigured room for collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: Union reports that Learning Lab Room 232 has modular furniture for group collaboration and is available for student group study when library instruction is not scheduled.
cards.source_title: Learning Lab gets revamped | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Schaffer Library entrance requires a Union ID; scheduled library instruction classes take priority over group study.

cards.title: Viewing Stations
cards.subtitle: Schaffer Library, first floor
cards.notes: Work through a course film or DVD at a first-floor station; ask the Service Desk about Roku sticks or external disc drives.
cards.short_summary: Two first-floor media stations with TVs and DVD-capable computers.
cards.evidence_claim: Schaffer Library provides two first-floor viewing stations with TVs, Roku-stick compatibility, and computers with DVD drives for the library DVD collection.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Schaffer Library entrance requires a Union ID; Roku sticks and external disc drives are available for checkout at the Library Service Desk.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on nearby Schenectady corridors, each with a specific documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Jay Street Marketplace
cards.subtitle: Jay Street pedestrian corridor
cards.notes: Walk the cobblestone pedestrian stretch and pause at the specialty shops and places to eat listed by Union.
cards.short_summary: A cobblestone shopping-and-food walk downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Union College describes Jay Street as a cobblestone walkway lined with specialty shops and places to eat.
cards.access_notes: Public pedestrian corridor; individual businesses set their own access and purchase terms.

cards.title: Movieland 6 Cinema
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the current listings, then plan a film outing with standard cinema concessions available on site.
cards.short_summary: A downtown cinema for current film screenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Union College identifies Movieland 6 Cinema as a place to catch current Hollywood films and buy concession items.
cards.access_notes: Confirm showtimes and ticket availability with the cinema before going.

cards.title: Tara Kitchen
cards.subtitle: Liberty Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s location page to confirm the Schenectady address and current dinner service before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in Moroccan restaurant on Liberty Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Tara Kitchen lists its Schenectady location at 431 Liberty Street and identifies it as walk-in service.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Tuesday–Sunday dinner service; verify before travel.

cards.title: Proctors
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor
cards.notes: Look at the performance calendar and choose a show; the building includes several theatres and a training center.
cards.short_summary: A multi-space performing-arts stop on State Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Proctors states that its building at 432 State Street contains several theatres, a training center, rental spaces and a café.
cards.access_notes: Performance admission and building access vary by event; consult the venue calendar.

cards.title: Schenectady Greenmarket
cards.subtitle: Jay Street / City Hall corridor
cards.notes: Check the market schedule, then browse local vendors for food and other goods in downtown Schenectady.
cards.short_summary: A local-vendor market near the Jay Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Union College identifies the Schenectady Greenmarket as a local shopping-and-eating option near campus.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current market date, location and vendors before visiting.

cards.title: Arthur's Market
cards.subtitle: North Ferry Street, beside the Stockade corridor
cards.notes: Pair a Stockade walk with a stop for coffee or baked goods, as suggested on Union’s local guide.
cards.short_summary: A Stockade-adjacent market stop for coffee and baked goods.
cards.evidence_claim: Union College’s Stockade recommendation specifically directs visitors to Arthur’s Market for coffee and baked goods.
cards.access_notes: Food and beverage purchases are optional; confirm current service before visiting.

cards.title: Mohawk-Hudson Bike-Hike Trail
cards.subtitle: Riverfront and Washington Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Enter from a suitable access point and follow the route through the county, including the downtown and riverfront sections.
cards.short_summary: A regional trail that links downtown, riverfront and historic-route segments.
cards.evidence_claim: Schenectady County says the trail runs through downtown’s business and entertainment district and includes a riverfront ALCO Heritage Trail section.
cards.source_title: Empire State Trail/Mohawk-Hudson Bike-Hike Trail | Schenectady County
cards.access_notes: Use the county trail map and follow posted route, etiquette and street-crossing guidance.

cards.title: Schenectady Historical Museum
cards.subtitle: Washington Avenue, Stockade corridor
cards.notes: Start at the museum to explore Schenectady County history through exhibits, programs or a scheduled Stockade walking tour.
cards.short_summary: A history-museum starting point in the Stockade.
cards.evidence_claim: The Schenectady County Historical Society describes its museum as a starting point for exploring county history through programs and exhibits.
cards.source_title: Museum & Library - Schenectady County Historical Society
cards.access_notes: The museum lists admission and hours; library research appointments must be scheduled in advance.

cards.title: Central Park Rose Garden
cards.subtitle: Central Park / Rugby Road corridor
cards.notes: Take a garden walk, stay on paths and respect the plantings, water features, sculptures and other public visitors.
cards.short_summary: A public rose garden inside Central Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Schenectady lists a Rose Garden among Central Park’s features, and its garden rules state that it is open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Public access is documented; photography-for-hire and rentals have separate city permit or fee rules.

cards.title: Robb Alley
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor, inside Proctors
cards.notes: Pass through the public alley connecting State Street, the box office and Apostrophe Café while you explore the Proctors block.
cards.short_summary: A public passage through the Proctors building.
cards.evidence_claim: Proctors describes Robb Alley as a public space with access from State Street, the box office and Apostrophe Café.
cards.access_notes: Access may be affected by venue operations or events; check with Proctors if planning a specific visit.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Union College gatherings, ceremonies, sounds, and service traditions tied to campus life in Schenectady.

cards.title: Open the year at Convocation
cards.subtitle: September · Union College
cards.notes: Attend the community gathering that welcomes the new class, recognizes Dean’s List students, includes music, and ends with a community barbecue.
cards.short_summary: Union’s official opening-of-year ceremony combines welcome, recognition, music, and a barbecue.
cards.evidence_claim: Union identifies Convocation as the official start of the academic year, with the full community welcoming the new class, musical performances, Dean’s List recognition, and a concluding barbecue.
cards.access_notes: See Union’s current events and orientation information for attendance details.

cards.entity_name: John Calvin Toll Day of Community Engagement
cards.title: Join Toll Day’s community work
cards.subtitle: Fall service tradition · Schenectady and Capital Region
cards.notes: Register through the Kenney Center when offered, then work with local partners on ongoing projects while learning about community needs and culture.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding Union service day connecting campus volunteers with regional community projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Union calls John Calvin Toll Day of Community Engagement a longtime College tradition in which students work alongside local community members on projects across the region.
cards.source_title: Annual Events | Kenney Center | Union College
cards.access_notes: Participation depends on the annual program and project registration.

cards.title: Return for Homecoming and Family Weekend
cards.subtitle: October · Union College
cards.notes: Use the annual schedule to choose campus activities, food events, and the featured game; invite family or attend with friends as programming permits.
cards.short_summary: Union’s fall gathering blends family programming, campus activities, and a featured athletic game.
cards.evidence_claim: Union describes Homecoming and Family Weekend as an annual autumn gathering of the Union community with food, activities, and the anticipated big game.
cards.access_notes: Consult the current Homecoming and Family Weekend schedule for event-specific access.

cards.title: Mark the charter anniversary on Founders Day
cards.subtitle: February · Union College
cards.notes: Look for the annual program featuring a keynote, student musical performances, and recognition of educational accomplishments across the College.
cards.short_summary: The College commemorates its charter anniversary with talks, student music, and recognition.
cards.evidence_claim: Union states that Founders Day commemorates the anniversary of the College’s charter and features a distinguished keynote, student music, and recognition of accomplishments.
cards.access_notes: Check the annual Founders Day announcement for location and attendance information.

cards.title: See campus turn into ReUnion weekend
cards.subtitle: May · Union College
cards.notes: Follow the yearly ReUnion program for receptions, picnics, the parade, fireworks, and opportunities to reconnect across Union generations.
cards.short_summary: Union’s alumni-and-campus reunion weekend includes social events, a parade, picnics, and fireworks.
cards.evidence_claim: Union describes ReUnion as a weekend for alumni, students, faculty, staff, and friends with receptions, picnics, a parade, fireworks, and other activities.
cards.access_notes: Event access and any registration requirements vary by the annual ReUnion program.

cards.title: Watch the Commencement procession through the Nott
cards.subtitle: June · Nott Memorial and Schaffer Library
cards.notes: Use the College’s commencement information to view the ceremony, including the graduating procession through the Nott Memorial’s western door.
cards.short_summary: Graduates process through the Nott Memorial’s western door for Union’s June Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Union states that its June Commencement ceremonies, held in front of Schaffer Library, include a spirited procession through the Nott Memorial’s western door.
cards.access_notes: Follow the current Commencement schedule and campus access guidance.

cards.title: Volunteer at the Community Carnival
cards.subtitle: Union College campus · Schenectady
cards.notes: Sign up with the Kenney Center to help run games, crafts, sports, food service, or setup and cleanup for local families at this campus event.
cards.short_summary: A Union tradition that welcomes local families for games, crafts, sports, food, and volunteering.
cards.evidence_claim: Union calls Community Carnival a College tradition inviting local families to a free on-campus event with food, games, crafts, sports, and more.
cards.source_title: Annual Events | Kenney Center | Union College
cards.access_notes: The Kenney Center lists volunteer needs and annual event details.

cards.title: Spend a day with the Steinmetz Symposium
cards.subtitle: Annual student research and creative-work celebration
cards.notes: Review the current program, then attend presentations and displays that showcase Union students’ scholarly and creative work across disciplines.
cards.short_summary: Union’s interdisciplinary symposium highlights student research and creative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Union’s Steinmetz Symposium program identifies the event as an interdisciplinary tradition and celebration, established in 1991 to showcase student scholarly and creative work.
cards.access_notes: Use the current Steinmetz program for session times, locations, and attendance details.

cards.title: Listen for Memorial Chapel’s mechanical chimes
cards.subtitle: Memorial Chapel · Union College
cards.notes: Pause near Memorial Chapel during the day to hear the chimes, then look for special-occasion performances when the College announces them.
cards.short_summary: Union maintains mechanical Memorial Chapel bells as a century-old campus sound tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Union reports that Memorial Chapel’s chimes have sounded since the building opened in 1925 and that the College maintains mechanical bells rather than recordings or synthesizers.
cards.source_title: Soundtrack of a century: College chimes still sound a sweet note across campus | Union College
cards.access_notes: The chimes ring automatically; special manual performances depend on College programming.

cards.entity_name: Ode to Old Union President’s House Serenade
cards.title: Sing “Ode to Old Union” at the President’s House
cards.subtitle: Orientation tradition · President’s House
cards.notes: If included in orientation, gather with classmates at the President’s House and follow the program’s invitation to serenade the president with the alma mater.
cards.short_summary: Orientation programming brings students to the President’s House to sing Union’s alma mater.
cards.evidence_claim: Union’s Fall 2026 orientation schedule describes gathering at the President’s House to serenade President Kiss with “Ode to Old Union” as the return of a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: This is listed in the Fall 2026 orientation schedule; participation is tied to orientation programming.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Union College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, campus-centered sequence for getting oriented, finding recurring student activities, and sampling Union’s study, arts, and outdoor spaces.

cards.title: Start at the Nott Memorial
cards.subtitle: Campus landmark · center of campus
cards.notes: Use the Nott as a first landmark, then look for its current talks, readings, special events, or gallery displays before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A central landmark that also hosts academic and arts programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Union identifies the Nott Memorial as a National Historic Landmark that hosts talks, readings, special events, and Mandeville Gallery exhibits.
cards.access_notes: Check the campus calendar or gallery information for a specific event or exhibit.

cards.title: Take a daylight lap through Jackson’s Garden
cards.subtitle: Eight-acre campus garden
cards.notes: Walk the garden paths in daylight and pause at the creek, sculptures, gazebo, or gingko reading nook for a relaxed first look at campus.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped campus walk with gardens, creek crossings, and outdoor art.
cards.evidence_claim: Union describes Jackson’s Garden as an eight-acre campus garden with herb, flower, and evergreen gardens, a creek, sculptures, and a gazebo.
cards.access_notes: Visit during daylight and stay on established garden paths.

cards.title: Get your bearings at Reamer
cards.subtitle: Campus center · dining and student offices
cards.notes: Make Reamer your practical stop for food, mail, student offices, WRUC, and flyers or announcements that point to the week’s activities.
cards.short_summary: The campus hub combines dining, student services, media, and gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: Union says Reamer Campus Center houses dining services, student resources and offices, WRUC, and the student newspaper.
cards.access_notes: Dining and office availability varies; confirm hours and access before visiting.

cards.title: Use UEngage to choose one open event
cards.subtitle: Union student-event platform
cards.notes: Browse UEngage for a current event, then try one club meeting or program; Union says recognized clubs follow an all-comers participation policy.
cards.short_summary: A direct way to find a scheduled student activity without guessing what is happening.
cards.evidence_claim: Union identifies UEngage as the platform student groups use to advertise events and says its clubs have an all-comers policy.
cards.access_notes: Availability depends on the event listing; review its details and any registration requirements.

cards.title: Find a study perch at Schaffer Library
cards.subtitle: Library · Learning Commons and Writing Center
cards.notes: Choose a reading nook, carrel, workstation, or Learning Commons table, and save the Writing Center location for when your first assignments arrive.
cards.short_summary: A study-and-research stop with varied work spaces and peer writing support.
cards.evidence_claim: Union says Schaffer Library includes the Learning Commons, study spaces, and the Writing Center.
cards.access_notes: A Union ID is required to enter; during term, posted building hours run until midnight Friday and Saturday and 2 a.m. Sunday.

cards.title: Check what’s on view at Mandeville Gallery
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Nott Memorial
cards.notes: Look up the current exhibition, then pair a gallery visit with time in the Nott rather than assuming a particular show will be running.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art gallery located inside Union’s signature building.
cards.evidence_claim: Union states that Mandeville Gallery is on the second floor of the Nott Memorial and exhibits nationally recognized contemporary artists.
cards.source_title: Collections and Exhibitions | Schaffer Library | Union College
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current exhibition and public access information before visiting.

cards.title: See whether Yulman has a student production
cards.subtitle: Theater and Dance complex
cards.notes: Check the department calendar for a production, staged reading, or monologue, then plan around the posted performance details and ticket instructions.
cards.short_summary: A campus theater complex for major student productions and flexible staged work.
cards.evidence_claim: Union says Yulman Theater includes a Main Stage for major student productions and a Black Box Theater for staged readings and monologues.
cards.access_notes: Programming and ticket requirements vary by production; consult Theater and Dance listings.

cards.title: Listen for a Memorial Chapel performance
cards.subtitle: Campus chapel · choral and orchestral venue
cards.notes: Check whether a choral or orchestral performance is scheduled, and arrive with enough time to admire the building before the program begins.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus venue known for ceremonies and acoustic performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Union says Memorial Chapel is used for choral and orchestral performances as well as key College ceremonies.
cards.access_notes: Events are schedule-dependent; verify start time, admission, and access with the presenting organization.

cards.title: Catch the Film Club’s weekend movie
cards.subtitle: Recurring on-campus film activity
cards.notes: Look for the Film Club’s weekend screening listing and invite someone from your orientation group; the club presents films on campus each weekend of term.
cards.short_summary: A recurring, on-campus movie option spanning popular, classic, foreign, and fine-art films.
cards.evidence_claim: Union says Film Club selects current films shown on campus free of charge each weekend of the term.
cards.source_title: Clubs & Organizations | Student Activities | Union College
cards.access_notes: Check UEngage or Film Club announcements for the current title, time, and screening location.

cards.title: Plan ahead with the Outing Club
cards.subtitle: Student outdoor-activity club
cards.notes: Ask about the next supervised trip and its preparation requirements; the club runs several weekend activities each term and supplies most equipment.
cards.short_summary: A student club offering organized outdoor trips beyond campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Union says its Outing Club sponsors canoeing, cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, hiking, rock climbing, and spelunking, with trips several weekends each term.
cards.source_title: Clubs & Organizations | Student Activities | Union College
cards.access_notes: Participate only through the club’s organized trip and follow its trip-specific safety and equipment guidance.

warnings: Specific event schedules, admission, and access can change; verify current listings before attending.
